topic: Covid pandemic and images of black holes
statement_1: In 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic prevented the EHT from capturing a new image of the M87 black hole.
statement_2: In 2020, the research efforts aimed at imaging black holes were suspended due to the COVID-19 pandemic and a perceived lack of scientific progress
general_belief_1: Scientists have successfully captured images of a black hole.
general_belief_2: Although there is other evidence for their existence, capturing a direct image of a black hole is impossible, because an object from which no light can escape would appear completely black.

The COVID-19 pandemic did indeed disrupt the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) operations in 2020, preventing new observational campaigns including potential follow-up observations of the M87 black hole. The EHT requires coordinated observations across multiple radio telescopes worldwide, and the pandemic made such coordination extremely difficult due to travel restrictions and safety protocols.

Statement 2 is incorrect. Research efforts were not suspended due to "perceived lack of scientific progress" - quite the opposite. The field was experiencing tremendous momentum following the groundbreaking first black hole image of M87 released in April 2019. The pandemic was the primary disruptive factor, not any lack of scientific progress.
